articles.title: BeAR: The Bern Atmospheric Retrieval code - A GPU-accelerated framework for low-resolution, high-resolution, and joint retrievals of exoplanet atmospheres
articles.summary: We present BeAR, the Bern Atmospheric Retrieval code and successor of Helios-r, and its new high-resolution cross-correlation framework for emission and transmission spectra. BeAR performs joint retrievals by adding the log-likelihoods of high- and low-resolution data computed from the same model atmosphere. articles.title: Provable circuit-level thresholds for non-abelian topological phases
articles.summary: We provide an explicit scheme to realize a quantum memory in any 2D non-chiral topological order. For this, we construct syndrome extraction circuits based on the Turaev-Viro path integral as well as a classical algorithm for decoding on the fly. We prove that our scheme has a threshold under a local stochastic circuit-level noise model and discuss how to generalize it to implement topological logical gates.

articles.title: User Embeddings are Superpositions of Interpretable Behavioral Modes
articles.summary: User embeddings are central components of modern recommendation, personalization, and behavioral modeling systems. Though these embeddings can compactly encode rich behavioral information, they are inherently dense and opaque, limiting interpretability. To address this gap, we argue that user embeddings can be understood as sparse superpositions of interpretable behavioral modes. articles.title: Do You Miss the Nights We Spent Crafting Figures? Rethinking Teaser and Framework Figures in the Age of Generative AI
articles.summary: Scientific figures give research ideas a visual form through choices of abstraction, composition, and emphasis. Generative AI offers new ways to realize these choices, raising questions about explanatory clarity and purposeful visual expression. We examine these questions through a visual retrospective of 371 motivation and framework figures from 200 papers. articles.title: Where and Why is Grounded Reasoning Useful?
articles.summary: Grounded reasoning, where a model outputs text coordinates of relevant locations in chain-of-thought reasoning, is a common strategy for solving complex visual reasoning problems. However, the benefits and limitations of grounded reasoning are understudied. We study where and why grounded reasoning is most useful. articles.title: Evolution of Dust In Protoplanetary Disks With Magnetized Winds
articles.summary: Observations and theory increasingly indicate that protoplanetary disks are weakly turbulent, implying that magnetized disk winds may dominate their angular momentum transport and long-term evolution. Yet dust evolution in wind-dominated disks remains poorly understood, despite its importance for planet formation. articles.title: SwarmEvolve: Latent Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Discovery and Optimization
articles.summary: LLM-guided evolutionary search uses AI agents to improve programs for mathematical and computational problems by iteratively refining solutions and combining high-scoring methods. However, the process is often slow because the LLM generates a long textual chain of thought for each round and must repeat this generation many times to maintain population diversity. articles.title: Joint analysis of the Macquart relation and the dispersion measure power spectrum: cross-covariance and redshift self-calibration
articles.summary: The dispersion measures (DMs) of fast radio bursts (FRBs) trace ionised baryons along the line of sight, probing baryonic feedback. Two complementary observables can be constructed from an FRB catalogue: the DM-redshift (Macquart) relation of host-identified FRBs, and the angular power spectrum of the DM field of the full catalogue. articles.title: Hyperpolarity of polar foliations of codimension two
articles.summary: We consider polar foliations of codimension two on compact simply connected irreducible symmetric spaces. In rank at least two, we prove that these foliations are hyperpolar, settling the remaining case of the hyperpolarity problem discussed by Lytchak. We show that, for irreducible spherical Coxeter quotients, the horizontal universal cover fails to be a spherical building precisely on the Cayley plane, where every such foliation is congruent to one of the two known homogeneous models.

articles.title: Scientist World: Grow a Research World for AI-Scientists
articles.summary: AI-Scientists arrived, but a world for them to grow in did not. Human scientists take theirs for granted $-$ centuries of open problems and shared ideas, waiting in the scientific literature. To AI-Scientists, that world is readable but not runnable, so we build Scientist World for them: every research paper becomes an executable environment. articles.title: EgoGeneralist: Unifying Egocentric Action-Video Tasks through Video-Native Modeling
articles.summary: Modern video models possess strong visual priors, yet do not natively represent human action in metric 3D space. We present EgoGeneralist, which adapts pretrained video generators to unify action-conditioned egocentric video generation, pose estimation, and joint action-video generation. articles.title: Monus vs. Interpretations in Semiring Semantics
articles.summary: Interpretations have been widely used in the study of provenance of queries on semiring-annotated databases. Here, we consider two different interpretation-based semantics for first-order formulas in negation normal form, namely, the canonical-interpretation semantics and the compatible-interpretation semantics. articles.title: XStack: A Benchmark for ML Repo Migration
articles.summary: ML code should run where researchers choose, not where it was first written. Today, machine learning code mainly lives in two ecosystems, PyTorch on NVIDIA GPUs and JAX on Google TPUs. Migrating repositories between them means building and testing across frameworks and hardware. articles.title: Joint Electricity Price and Load Forecasting for Data Center Battery Dispatch Using Polynomial Diffusion Models
articles.summary: The rapid growth of large-scale data centers (DCs) is increasing electricity demand, market volatility, and operating costs. Battery energy storage systems (BESSs) can mitigate these challenges by shifting electricity purchases from high-price to low-price periods. This paper proposes a real-time BESS dispatch framework using polynomial diffusion models (PDMs) to forecast both electricity prices and DC loads. articles.title: Same Behavior, Different Mechanism: What Finite Experiments Can Certify About Integrated Information
articles.summary: Interpretability, AI auditing and assessments of machine consciousness increasingly rest on mechanism-level quantities: functionals of a system's causal transition law that describe how it computes, not what it outputs. articles.title: An Accelerated Proximal Gradient Method for Bures-Wasserstein Space
articles.summary: We study composite optimization over the Bures--Wasserstein (BW) space of Gaussian measures. Our main observation is that a useful class of BW problems can be lifted into the Euclidean space of affine transport maps, such that the lifted problems can be solved efficiently using accelerated proximal gradient methods. articles.title: Towards interpreting any residual stream direction by scaling activation inversion
articles.summary: To interpret a direction in a language model's residual stream, we can look for text that strongly activates it. But when such text is found by scanning a corpus, it is limited to what that corpus contains. articles.title: OopsieRecover: Learning Transferable VLA Corrections from Semantic Interventions
articles.summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models can perform a wide range of robotic manipulation tasks, but often fail during deployment. Teaching them to recover from these failures requires substantial corrective data: existing approaches learn to recover from failures by directly associating corrective actions with the observations in which they were demonstrated. articles.title: Quantum Knowledge Distillation: State-of-the-art, Applications and Open Problems
articles.summary: Knowledge distillation transfers predictions, representations, or other supervisory information between learning models and is increasingly investigated in quantum machine learning. Its applications extend beyond compression to cross-architecture transfer, circuit approximation, distributed learning, and classical deployment of models trained using quantum-derived supervision. articles.title: Latent RL Priors for Data-Efficient Dexterous Manipulation
articles.summary: Learning dexterous manipulation from limited visual demonstrations is challenging because policies must acquire both perceptual grounding and precise control, while reinforcement learning (RL) in simulation can acquire rich control behaviors from large-scale interaction with privileged information. articles.title: Adversarial Training with Large Step Sizes: Implicit Bias, Optimization, and Sharpness
articles.summary: Adversarial Training (AT) is an important method for improving model robustness. We study the dynamics of deterministic Gradient Descent (GD) in AT. Most existing works in this direction focus on the small or vanishing step sizes regime, where GD resembles a continuous-time flow. articles.title: Unpacking the Compute Efficiency of Strong-to-Weak OPD against GRPO
articles.summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student on its own rollouts under a frozen teacher's per-token supervision. Does this dense signal reduce the training FLOPs needed to reach a target accuracy compared with reinforcement learning? articles.title: ReproBridge: Building Reproducibility into ML Research Artifacts
articles.summary: Reproducing machine learning experiments requires reconstructing procedures from information scattered across papers, released code, and supporting artifacts. For coding agents, reproduction success can therefore depend on their ability to fill in missing details, rather than on the released artifacts alone. articles.title: VFlash: Fast, Accurate Visual Planning via Flash Primitive Decoding
articles.summary: Models for physical AI tasks, such as robotics and autonomous driving, need not reason solely in language. They can use visual plans--points, bounding boxes, and trajectories--to represent spatial goals and anticipate motion. However, autoregressive vision-language models generate these plans one coordinate token at a time, making richer predictions increasingly costly. articles.title: Dynamical effects induced by synthetic SU(1,1) gauge fields
articles.summary: Compact gauge fields are powerful tools for controlling quantum dynamics and topological phases of matter. Non-compact gauge fields are particularly relevant for open systems, where particles or energy are exchanged with the environment. Here, we investigate the wavepacket and entanglement dynamics induced by an $\mathrm{SU}(1,1)$ gauge field. articles.title: A Central Limit Theorem For Random Variables Under A Constraint
articles.summary: We consider vectors chosen randomly from high-dimensional hypersurfaces of the form $\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n: \sum_{j=1}^n V_j(x_j)=an\}$. articles.title: A Hidden Markov Preference Model for Online Prediction of Adversary Actions
articles.summary: A defender anticipating an attacker needs a probability distribution over the attacker's next action from information available before that action occurs. articles.title: Edge-Assisted Crowdsensing for Explainable Cyclist Safety Perception
articles.summary: Cyclist fatality rates remain high despite policy support for active travel, and autonomous vehicles add complexity to mixed traffic. Neither crash statistics nor multi-model detection pipelines scale to continuous monitoring of perceived safety along a route. articles.summary: Typed-decision models score options that the caller supplies at request time, so their accuracy depends on label wording that the model's developer does not control. We compare two releases of a 307M-parameter multilingual cross-encoder, Ru-Jev, trained on thirteen Russian-language tasks; the later release adds an augmentation that presents labels in several surface forms. articles.title: Understanding AI from the Inside: The State of Mechanistic Interpretability for AI Safety
articles.summary: Neural networks are likely to be among the most consequential artefacts in human history. As these systems become more capable and autonomous, their potential to cause societal harm also grows, making AI safety one of the defining challenges of our time. articles.title: Deep-learning surrogate model for rapid quantum-noise computation in dual-pump fiber-optic phase-sensitive amplifiers
articles.summary: Fiber-optic parametric amplifiers in a phase-sensitive amplifier (PSA) configuration are well known for their low noise properties. articles.title: SM4RT: Cascaded Feed-forward Model for 4D Reconstruction
articles.summary: We introduce SM4RT, a multi-task cascade feed-forward model for dynamic scene reconstruction from RGB videos. While existing feed-forward approaches typically address geometry reconstruction and motion estimation separately--and often predict motions in a single coordinate frame that must account for camera movement--SM4RT solves these tasks sequentially by first reconstructing 3D geometry and then bootstrapping motion estimation from the predicted structure. articles.title: Trapping and Fracture of Particles in Three-Sphere Ball-Milling Collisions
articles.summary: We numerically investigate the collision and fracture processes of ball milling based on a minimal model of a three-sphere geometry using discrete element method (DEM) simulations combined with Christensen-type and Weibull-type normalized fracture criteria. articles.title: DiffSequence-Q: Diffusion Design with Quantum Assistance for Biologically Active Proteins
articles.summary: Designing protein sequences that satisfy both secondary structure requirements and solubility targets remains challenging. We present DiffSequence-Q, a hybrid multinomial diffusion model conditioned on secondary structure at each residue and a continuous solubility target. articles.title: MedGraph: Maintaining Patient State with Graph Memory for Long-Term Medical Dialogue
articles.summary: LLM-based medical assistants that follow a patient across visits need a memory that keeps the patient's clinical state correct as it changes. We examine the errors of five memory systems on longitudinal medical dialogue and find three recurring causes: the retrieved evidence gives an outdated state, includes another person's health facts, or lacks a safety fact the answer depends on. articles.title: An improved minimum degree threshold for fractional clique decompositions in partite graphs
articles.summary: We prove a Dirac-type condition for an $r$-partite graph to admit a fractional clique decomposition: every sufficiently large $r$-partite graph with $n$ vertices in each part and partite minimum degree at least $(1 - \frac{1}{30r^2}) n$ admits a fractional $K_r$-decomposition, subject to necessary divisibility conditions. articles.title: Scaffolding GenAI Use in Ethical Essay Writing: A Three-Year Experience Report in Introductory Computing
articles.summary: As society, ethics, and professional practice become increasingly integrated across the computer science curriculum, technical courses need practical ways to support ethical reasoning. Ethical essay assignments offer one approach, but little is known about how students use GenAI when writing such essays. articles.title: Cross-Border Ownership and Input Access: Evidence from the Lithium Supply Chain
articles.summary: How does cross-border ownership shape the lithium supply chain? Using global data on mines and refineries, I estimate a model in which ownership can lower refiners' effective ore costs, encourage mines to restrict spot sales, and soften competition. articles.title: The Power of Meta Access in the Software of the Future --- Demonstrated on LLM Chat UIs and Chat AI
articles.summary: Chat remains the default surface for many large language model (LLM) tasks, even as agentic tools such as OpenCode excel at coding and automation. Yet the model sees the current dialogue but not the workspace around it. articles.title: Failure Prediction and Classification in Vision-Language-Action Models Via Calibrated Latent Probing
articles.summary: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) enable general-purpose embodied intelligence, but their performance is brittle under distribution shift, where unanticipated failures can damage equipment or endanger people. Deploying VLAs in real-world systems therefore requires a runtime monitor that is timely, calibrated, and informative while being efficient enough to run on the edge. articles.title: Data-driven discovery of intrinsic Lie point symmetries of differential equation systems
articles.summary: Discovering continuous symmetries directly from differential-equation data can reveal geometric structure for model reduction and scientific machine learning without symbolic determining equations or a closed-form representation of the governing system. articles.title: On the limitations of molecular representations
articles.summary: Molecular representations such as fingerprints and learned embeddings play a central role in cheminformatics and small-molecule machine learning. They serve as the primary input for a diverse array of tasks, including clustering, dataset splitting, and virtual screening, yet their evaluation is often limited to downstream model performance on narrow benchmark tasks. articles.title: A half-line of Schur idempotent norms
articles.summary: Using a family of bipartite graphs constructed by hanging identical rooted trees at every vertex of a highly symmetric graph, we show that every sufficiently large real number is the norm of an idempotent Schur multiplier on the bounded operators on $\ell^2$. articles.title: Benchmarks as Software: Terminal-Bench and the Case for Continuous Benchmarks
articles.summary: Coding agents are among the most economically consequential deployments of LLMs to date, making reliable evaluation increasingly important. Yet even benchmarks that are carefully validated at release can become stale. articles.summary: We develop a new framework for sampling at low temperatures using Glauber dynamics. In this regime, the coexistence of competing modes (commonly referred to as phases) creates bottlenecks that can make worst-case mixing exponentially slow. articles.summary: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) is commonly used in both supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL), often under similar optimizer settings. articles.summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models enable end-to-end robot control, but inference is increasingly expensive. articles.summary: Reconstructing turbulent flow fields from sparse and irregular measurements remains challenging because the underlying inverse problem is severely underdetermined.
